items.q: Nail-patella syndrome is inherited as and caused by:
items.exp: Nail-patella syndrome: AD, LMX1B mutation. (Book p785)

items.q: Match the nail-patella syndrome features — 1) Nails  2) Knee  3) Pelvis X-ray  4) Renal … A) Absent patella  B) Adolescent microhaematuria + proteinuria, usually benign  C) Dystrophic nails  D) Iliac horn
items.exp: Clinical features of nail-patella syndrome: dystrophic nails, absent patella, iliac horn, and renal manifestation — adolescent microhaematuria + proteinuria that is benign (rarely progresses to ESRD). (Book p785)

items.q: A 16-year-old has microhaematuria and mild proteinuria with absent patellae and dystrophic nails. A pelvic radiograph shows an iliac horn. The renal prognosis is:
opts: Benign — it rarely progresses to ESRD
Rapidly progressive to ESRD within weeks
items.exp: Renal manifestation of nail-patella syndrome: adolescent microhaematuria + proteinuria, benign, rarely progressing to ESRD. (Book p785)

items.q: Fill up: On X-ray, nail-patella syndrome shows an iliac ______.
items.exp: Nail-patella syndrome features include the iliac horn, shown in the pelvic radiograph labelled 'iliac horns'. (Book p785)

items.q: The investigation finding on electron microscopy in nail-patella syndrome is:
items.exp: Investigation in nail-patella syndrome: EM shows a moth-eaten appearance (figure 'moth eaten appearance'). (Book p785)

items.q: Match each familial glomerular syndrome with its electron-microscopy signature — 1) Alport syndrome  2) Thin GBM disease  3) Nail-patella syndrome … A) Uniformly thin basement membrane (<200–300 nm)  B) Moth-eaten appearance  C) Splitting + lamellation of lamina densa (basket weave)
items.exp: EM signatures: Alport → splitting/lamellation of the lamina densa with basket-weave and alternate thick/thin foci; thin GBM disease → uniformly thin (<200–300 nm); nail-patella → moth-eaten appearance. (Book p785)

items.q: Dystrophic nails and an absent patella are clinical features of nail-patella syndrome along with an iliac horn.
opts: False — dystrophic nails belong to Alport syndrome
False — the absent patella is seen in Fabry disease
True, but the iliac horn occurs only in Alport syndrome
items.exp: Nail-patella syndrome features: dystrophic nails, absent patella, iliac horn and renal (adolescent microhaematuria + proteinuria, benign). (Book p785)

items.q: Nail-patella syndrome's renal involvement (adolescent microhaematuria + proteinuria) is classified as:
opts: Nephrotic — progresses in all cases by 5 years
items.exp: Renal manifestation of nail-patella syndrome: adolescent microhaematuria + proteinuria — benign (rarely progress to ESRD). (Book p785)

items.q: All but one of the following belong to nail-patella syndrome. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Anterior lenticonus is the pathognomonic ocular sign of Alport syndrome; nail-patella syndrome shows dystrophic nails, absent patella, iliac horn and benign renal involvement. (Book p785)
